kinds.about: HD texture packs: one folder per game id (the 6-character id, or its first 3 characters for every region) holding the pack's tex1_*.png or .dds files in any subfolders, as Dolphin's Load/Textures/<game id>.
kinds.doc: Dolphin 2606a looks for Load/Textures/<game id>, else the 3-character id (HiresTextures.cpp:196-214), and walks it as the root of a recursive search for .png and .dds (:97-98, FileSearch.cpp:66-77), so a linked game folder is followed; nothing writes there (dumps go to Dump/Textures, CommonPaths.h:61-63). HiresTextures is on only while a pack is installed; CacheHiresTextures stays False, which would read every texture at boot (:126-131). GFX.ini is global: with no pack Dolphin checks two folder names and loads nothing.

mods.doc: Dormant until a pack is placed: the library is <paths.mods>/dolphin/textures/<game id>, one link per game folder into ${state_root}/dolphin-user/Load/Textures, for GameCube and Wii alike.

render_scale.doc: GFX.ini [Settings] InternalResolution is Dolphin's EFB scale (Config::GFX_EFB_SCALE; 1 native, 2 is 1280x1056 for a 640x528 EFB), read at boot. While a game runs Dolphin steps it on its own hotkeys, Internal Resolution/Increase IR and Decrease IR (HotkeyScheduler.cpp:386-398 at c77bbaa0: one step each, never below native from 2), which the profile binds to Alt+F9 and Alt+F10: Semu types the steps between the running scale and the chosen one, paced as Dolphin's 5 ms hotkey poll needs (press_ms, gap_ms), so a new scale applies live and is saved for the next boot. Dolphin draws the picture letterboxed into its window at the window's size whatever the scale, so the renderer cuts it at the declared native 640x480 and keeps the window's picture when the scale is above 1x.

doc.runtime: Linux executes the pinned source-built Dolphin package from the bundle asset root; macOS runs the Dolphin.app from the same pin.
doc.rendering: OpenGL is forced in the managed profile. render_preload composes Semu's bezel and shader at the swap, reading the emulator's back buffer and writing the composed frame back: on Linux libsemupreload at the SDL/EGL swap, on macOS the window shim at -[NSOpenGLContext flushBuffer].
doc.user_directory: The explicit -u path keeps Dolphin's live Config tree under Semu's per-emulator state root on every platform.
doc.aspect: Each Wii output is a set of --config arguments (platforms.<os>.outputs.wii, appended after args by the launcher). The standard output passes SYSCONF.IPL.AR=False: the Wii's default widescreen answer renders titles anamorphic 16:9, which the profile's CustomStretch 4:3 pin in GFX.ini would squash. The widescreen output passes SYSCONF.IPL.AR=True and moves the CustomStretch pin to 16:9 (Graphics.Settings.CustomAspectRatioWidth/Height), so a 16:9 title draws the SEMU_RENDER_ASPECT rectangle the 16:9 TV cuts. SYSCONF lives in the seeded NAND, not an INI, so the command-line layer is the only route; Dolphin writes it into the session's SYSCONF at boot (BootManager) and GameCube boots ignore it. The command-line layer sits below game INIs (Enums.h SEARCH_ORDER puts LocalGame and GlobalGame first), so a GameSettings INI that sets the aspect would win; none shipped with 2606a or seeded by Semu does. The output is chosen per game (visual.games.wii.<game>.output), so a 4:3 title is never stretched by another game's 16:9 choice; switching it restarts the game.
doc.playlist: Dolphin 2606a reads .m3u and .m3u8 itself (Boot.cpp ReadM3UFile), resolving entries against the playlist's folder, so it receives the .m3u unchanged (playlist.open native). Core.AutoDiscChange in the profile lets it insert the next entry when the game asks for another disc.
doc.content: What Dolphin c77bbaa0 boots, by its last suffix (Source/Core/Core/Boot/Boot.cpp:212 playlists, 238-240 disc images and executables, 268 .dff, 271 .wad, 278 .json mod descriptors). No archive: a .zip or .7z ends in "Could not recognize file". The .m3u here is what lets its playlist.open stay native.

save_states.doc: Dolphin's selected slot runs 1-10 and wraps both ways (DolphinQt/MainWindow.cpp:1582-1596 at c77bbaa); Qt.ini starts each launch on slot 1 (profile.json doc.save_states).

menu.doc: Seen 2026-10-03 in the podman VM (tests/integration/menu-pause.sh with openbox, Animal Crossing through libsemupreload on llvmpipe): Ctrl+P (Toggle Pause) froze the title screen, and a menu record written while paused stayed invisible until Ctrl+P resumed it, so a paused Dolphin presents nothing. The Semu menu therefore opens over the running game, and on Linux it holds the pad while it is open (EVIOCGRAB once every pad is at rest, released after the closing press), so the game sees none of the menu's input; taps and Steam's radial keys still reach it. Without a window manager Dolphin took no hotkey at all (HotkeysRequireFocus), which gamescope never causes. The Wii Remote and its extensions read that same SDL pad (profile.json doc.wiimote), so the hold covers Wii games too; only the Deck's motion sensors, read raw through hidraw, still reach the game under the menu.

players.doc: Four Wii Remotes and four GameCube pads (Dolphin.ini SIDevice0-3, WiimoteSource0-3); profile.json renders one row per player.

controllers.doc: A live layout switch copies the player's stored profile (store, rendered at launch per player and layout) over the one file Semu keeps in Dolphin's Wiimote profile folder (active), then types that player's Next Profile chord (profile.json layout_hotkeys). Dolphin lists that folder recursively and sorted at every press and keeps one index for all remotes (InputProfile.cpp:56-71), so with Semu's file alone in it every switch is one press that lands on it whatever the index was: nothing to track, and a lost press changes nothing (press again). Other files there (the owner's own profiles) are counted and the index tracked from the launch, where Dolphin starts at 0. The names in retired, the files Semu's older releases generated there, are moved once to retired_directory (never over a file, never deleted). Dolphin polls hotkeys every 5 ms and needs a release between presses (HotkeyScheduler.cpp:149-156), so each press is held press_ms and followed by gap_ms, at least 30 each (the checker). The keys go to the game's X display through XTest when the supervisor reads keys there (Game Mode's Xwayland), else through Semu's uinput keyboard. A layout row with connection disconnected (GameCube) is a Wii Remote with nothing bound that the game sees leave: after its profile the supervisor types that player's Connect Wii Remote chord (profile.json connection_hotkeys) once, and once more on the way back after the bound profile, keeping each player's link as Dolphin left it (linked at boot whatever the layout).
